_comment: Which checks are required to merge, as this repository intends them. The authority is the
'main protection' ruleset in GitHub's settings; this file is the copy that lives in the repo,
so the intent is reviewable in a pull request rather than only visible to whoever can open the
It exists because six documents claim a number of required checks and nothing counted it. The
claim said ten while nine were enforced - Tests ran and passed on every pull request but was
not in the ruleset, so a pull request with a failing test suite could have merged. Nobody
noticed, because the number is prose. See #152.
tools/check_docs.py reads this file and enforces three things: that the documented count
matches it, that every entry sourced from ci.yml names a job that exists, and that every job
in ci.yml is either required or listed under not_required with a reason. That last one is the
part that would have caught the original defect - a job cannot quietly exist without being a
What it cannot check is whether GitHub's ruleset still matches this file. That needs the API.
Run tools/check_docs.py --ruleset to compare them; it needs gh and a token that can read

not_required.reason: Convenience only - it assigns the pull request and has no opinion about the change. Requiring it would block merges on an assignment step, and it is skipped on forks by design.

Runs on a weekly schedule and on demand, never on a pull request. It clones a separate repository over the network, so requiring it would make a merge wait on the wiki's state and on ci.yml losing the offline guarantee that keeps it from failing for reasons unrelated to the change under review.
